source: "The Education of a Libertarian," Cato Unbound, Apr. 13, 2009

text: Since 1920, the vast increase in welfare beneficiaries and the extension of the franchise to women — two constituencies that are notoriously tough for libertarians — have rendered the notion of 'capitalist democracy' into an oxymoron.
speaker: Peter Thiel
source: "The Education of a Libertarian," Cato Unbound

text: Our enemy is stagnation... anti-merit, anti-ambition, anti-striving, anti-achievement, anti-greatness.
speaker: Marc Andreessen

text: Our enemy is bureaucracy, vetocracy, gerontocracy, blind deference to tradition. Our enemy is corruption, regulatory capture, monopolies, cartels.
speaker: Marc Andreessen

text: We are not primitives, cowering in fear of the lightning bolt. We are the apex predator; the lightning works for us.
speaker: Marc Andreessen

text: It's a war. It's like when Hitler invaded Poland in 1939.
speaker: Stephen Schwarzman
source: remark to a nonprofit board on the carried-interest tax proposal, July 2010; first reported by Jonathan Alter, Newsweek, Aug. 15, 2010 (he later apologized)

text: The rights and interests of the laboring man will be protected and cared for—not by the labor agitators, but by the Christian men to whom God in His infinite wisdom has given the control of the property interests of the country.
speaker: George F. Baer
source: letter to W.F. Clark, on Philadelphia & Reading letterhead, July 17, 1902, during the anthracite coal strike (Baer later denied the letter's authenticity)

text: We are not politicians or public thinkers; we are the rich; we own America; we got it, God knows how, but we intend to keep it.
speaker: Frederick Townsend Martin
source: The Passing of the Idle Rich
